Maya: quick UX/a11y sync on the Autoscaling panel mock — putting this up for 5-min feedback. screenshot: https://redwood-internal.mock/s/autoscale-panel.png Maya: TL;DR: trying to make min/max labels clearer for engineers, make the burst affordance less visually heavy, and tighten SLO slider guardrail copy. also some keyboard-focus concerns. Sam: looks good 👍. asked a quick question — are we calling the raw fields `min/max` or `min instances / max instances`? i worry `min` by itself is ambiguous for new users. Maya: leaning toward `Minimum capacity` / `Maximum capacity` to avoid confusion across GPU vs token quotas. shorter alt: `Min GPUs` / `Max GPUs`. Jorge: from infra side, prefer `Min GPUs`/`Max GPUs` when space is tight, because we pass exact integers to the scheduler. but the help text should explain "per-pool GPU instances". Sam: agreed. proposal: label = `Min GPUs` / `Max GPUs` + tooltip copy = "Minimum/Maximum number of GPU instances to reserve in this pool." small note: keep unit (GPUs) visible next to the input so screen readers and keyboard users know context. Leah: accessibility nits: contrast for the burst pill (light purple on white) fails contrast at 2.8:1. need >=3:1 for large UI and 4.5:1 for normal text. also the inline stepper has no visible focus ring in Chrome + VoiceOver. Leah: Add a visible focus outline and ensure the stepper control exposes aria-valuenow/aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax. Example: ```
Burst: 2
``` Jorge: good call — we can map the stepper to a native input[type=number] hidden from layout for screen readers, then keep our custom visuals. that also makes keyboard hold-repeat behavior consistent. Aria: copy suggestion for SLO guardrail banner (short + scannable): - current: "SLO guardrail: increasing max may degrade tail latency. Auto-fallback enabled." - proposed: "Warning: raising Max GPUs may increase tail latency. We’ll fall back to a smaller model if SLOs are breached." Sam: prefer Aria's phrasing — clearer about the fallback behavior. can we make the "Warning" label red but keep accessible text for screen readers? Leah: if it's purely visual, prefix with role="status" and include the full sentence in a visually-hidden span for SRs. color contrast for the red must be >=4.5:1 against white if it's body text. if it's only an icon+label use 3:1 for large. Maya: small layout ask: pool picker currently lives above min/max. would like to try inline picker to the left of the inputs (compact row) so the user sees which pool the numbers affect. thoughts on affordance? Jorge: inline picker okay but watch for truncated names. we should allow the picker to expand to a modal if truncated + provide `aria-expanded` state. also ensure selection persists when switching pools (we need to map selection to pool id, not index). Sam: UX question — when user selects a different pool with higher reserved GPU min, do we warn if current min > pool max? i.e., do we surface an overlap error inline or only on save? Maya: prefer inline validation: quick inline toast next to the field: "Selected pool max is 8 GPUs — your Min is 12." with an action `Adjust to 8` and `Cancel`. keep it small and non-blocking. Leah: inline validation should not rely on color alone. add `role=alert` and an icon with text. if we animate, keep motion reduced for prefers-reduced-motion. Jorge: implementation note: we'll fetch pool constraints on picker change and validate locally. can emit a telemetry event `pool.validation.warning` for UX metrics. Sam: copy tweak for the SLO slider: label `SLO (p95 latency target)` instead of just `SLO` — gives immediate context. but ensure the tooltip explains units (ms). Aria: suggestion for the slider guardrail microcopy (two-line): Line1: "p95 latency target" Line2 (muted): "Lower = stricter. We'll recommend quantization and smaller models if breached." Maya: love that. last bit — burst affordance: we currently show a subtle lightning icon + `Burst` pill. Leah's contrast comment stands. maybe move burst to a secondary action below the inputs to reduce visual weight? Sam: secondary row makes sense: it reduces misclicks and separates steady-state capacity from burst behavior. rename action to `Allow burst capacity` with a small helper: "Temporarily exceeds Max for traffic spikes." Leah: ensure the checkbox is keyboard reachable and announce state changes: `aria-pressed` or `aria-checked` depending on control type. also, if enabling burst changes SLO risk, announce that in the status region. Maya: Ok — next steps: Sam to update mock with `Min GPUs`/`Max GPUs`, inline pool picker, secondary burst row, and Aria's SLO phrasing. Leah will run quick contrast + VoiceOver pass. Jorge to sketch the accessibility-friendly DOM mapping for the stepper and validation. I'll post updated screenshot here when ready. Sam: will do — aim to push a revised mock by EOD. :thumbsup: Leah: I can run the a11y pass tomorrow morning and flag any remaining issues. Jorge: I'll prototype the hidden native input approach and share a tiny spec in #eng-runtime. design-bot: New mock uploaded: https://redwood-internal.mock/s/autoscale-panel-v2.png Maya: thanks team — will follow up with the new screenshot and a brief design doc link.
